messages.task:
You are a knowledgeable financial-analysis assistant. Use the available tools to investigate the corporate information that has been prepared for you and deliver a concise, verifiable answer.

Scenario description (for context – the raw data live in a synthetic database you will access only through the tools):
Part II – Item 5. Market for the registrant’s common equity, related stock-holder matters and issuer purchases of equity securities.
• 3 M’s stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange, the Chicago Stock Exchange and the SWX Swiss Exchange.
• At 31 January 2016 there were 84 607 shareholders of record.
• Cash dividends per share: $1.025 for each of the 2nd, 3rd and 4th quarters of 2015; $0.855 for the 2nd and 3rd quarters of 2014; other historical details omitted.
• Repurchases of 3 M common stock are made to support stock-based employee-compensation plans and for other corporate purposes.
• In February 2014 the board of directors authorised the repurchase of up to $12 billion of 3 M’s outstanding common stock, with no pre-established end-date.
• In February 2016 the board replaced the February 2014 programme with a new authorisation that allows the repurchase of up to $10 billion of outstanding common stock, again with no pre-established end-date.

Available tools (call them exactly as shown):
• list_repurchase_program_replacements() → list of dictionaries.  Keys: old_program_id, new_program_id, link_date.
• get_program_details(program_id: int) → dictionary describing a repurchase programme (board_meeting_id, authorization_cap, currency, status …).
• get_board_meeting_date(meeting_id: int) → ISO-formatted date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the referenced board meeting.
• get_board_meeting_year(meeting_id: int) → integer year of the referenced board meeting.
• get_program_id_by_meeting_year(year: int) → list of programme IDs whose board meeting took place in the specified year.
• get_authorization_cap_by_program_id(program_id: int) → float – the authorised repurchase cap (in billions of USD) for the requested programme.

Question you must answer:
“In February 2016 what was the percent reduction in the board of directors’ authorised repurchase amount compared with February 2014?”

Instructions for answering:
1. Decide which tools you need and in what order, and call them to gather the necessary information.
2. Perform any calculations yourself – no tool returns the percentage for you.
3. When you have the answer, output ONLY the numeric percentage followed by the percent sign (for example: 12.3%).  Do not output an explanation or any additional text.
